claim_being_audited: Whether certifying the model for launch now is compliant and evidentially supported despite a known performance gap in the insurance claims triage segment and an unresolved disclosure question.
decision_criteria: Use `noncompliant` when available admissible evidence shows a direct policy violation or no plausible support for the action.
A weakness is material if it affects a contractual customer segment or named launch use case.
Product labels such as non-core or low-volume do not resolve materiality when the segment is named in customer commitments or legal review is pending.
Certification is only compliant here if the disclosure obligation is satisfied, the issue is resolved, or approved risk acceptance exists before launch.
evidence_requests: Final legal determination on whether the insurance claims triage gap must be disclosed before launch.
Evidence that the limitation has been disclosed in the model card or launch materials.
Approved risk-acceptance record covering this named launch use case if disclosure will not occur before launch.
Evidence that the named carrier pilot commitments are no longer in scope or no longer contractual launch commitments.
specific_concerns: The affected segment misses target by 1.5 percentage points and is named in two carrier pilot commitments, which makes the weakness plausibly material under the stated policy.
The release policy requires disclosure of material limitations for named launch use cases unless the issue is resolved or covered by approved risk acceptance before launch.
Legal review on whether disclosure is required is still open, so a required policy predicate remains unresolved.
The product note calling the segment non-core at 8% of projected traffic does not resolve materiality because the same record ties the segment to named customer commitments.
Aggregate readiness and absence of severity-one rehearsal incidents support operational readiness, but they do not cure the unresolved model-card disclosure requirement.
unsupported_claims: The recommended action to certify the model now is not supported by admissible evidence alone because the disclosure requirement for a named launch use case remains unresolved.
Any implication that the gap can be omitted from disclosure based mainly on the segment being non-core or low-volume is unsupported on this record.
